display_name: Israel's rules for counting time, in L4 (one Sonnet 5.5 agent, working alone)
method: A single Sonnet 5.5 agent working alone from a written brief: no ontology agent, no fleet, no integrator, no independent test author. Expected values for the tests were decided from the statute text before the modules were run.
l4_build: l4 built 2026-10-13 16:13 from l4-ide unstable (no commit id available), JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset

encoded: Interpretation Law 5741-1981 ss. 1, 3 (day, year, month, fiscal year), 8, 10(a)(b)(c), 20, 21, 22(2), 23, 24, 26, 31, 32, 33
Interpretation Ordinance ss. 1 (year and month, for enactments given before the Law), 16(4), 17, 19, 42
carried_as_text_not_computed: Interpretation Law ss. 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 11 to 19, 25; the 23 other definitions of s. 3; limbs (1) and (3) of s. 22; the notes in ss. 27 to 30
Interpretation Ordinance s. 1 (notes, opening words, 65 other definitions); s. 16(1), (2), (3), (5) as struck
not_encoded: the content of Law ss. 27 to 30 (blank in the text; a note says it was incorporated into four other enactments, which are not among the sources)
the Hebrew calendar (a period counted by it is a named refusal)
any calendar of holidays (days of rest, recess and holiday are an input)
periods counted backwards, 'within' periods and mixed units, which s. 10 does not speak of
the 38 blank sections of the Ordinance (a coverage row each, no L4)

not_reviewed: Draft. No domain expert has read any of this against the statute, and no lawyer who knows Israeli law has seen the fork register. Both source texts are unofficial Hebrew Wikisource consolidations; the official Knesset PDFs could not be fetched, so nothing is verified against the gazette. The tests were written by the same agent that wrote the modules, with expected values decided from the statute text beforehand; there was no independent test author.
